# R Packages Used in This Book {#sec-packages}

R comes with a large set of functions, called *base R*. Most of the work in this book also uses *packages*, collections of functions written by others and shared freely, mostly through CRAN, the Comprehensive R Archive Network. @sec-packages-intro explains how packages are installed and loaded. This appendix lists all the packages used in the book. It gives one install command for each part, so that you can install only what you need and start learning straight away.

## Packages by part {#sec-packages-list}

| Part | Packages | Used for |
|----------------|--------------------------|--------------------------------------|
| Throughout | `tidyverse` (including `dplyr`, `tidyr`, `readr`, `purrr`, `stringr`, `forcats`, `lubridate`, `ggplot2`, `tibble`) | Reading, transforming, reshaping and charting data |
| I. R Foundations | `purrr`, `magrittr`, `conflicted` | Functional programming, the older pipe, and handling clashing function names |
| II. Getting Data Ready | `digest`, `openssl`, `encryptr`, `readxl`, `writexl`, `openxlsx`, `janitor`, `pdftools`, `tidyxl`, `unpivotr`, `rvest`, `httr2`, `xml2`, `data.table`, `duckdb`, `dbplyr` | Protecting personal data, Excel, PDF and web pages, cleaning names, large data |
| III. Working with Text Fields | `rebus` | Readable regular expressions |
| IV. Exploring and Sampling | `scales`, `ggrepel`, `patchwork`, `RColorBrewer`, `colorspace`, `psych`, `skimr`, `GGally`, `PerformanceAnalytics`, `broom` | Charts and colour palettes, descriptive statistics and tidy test results |
| V. Forensic Tests | `validate`, `pointblank`, `benford.analysis`, `kableExtra`, `stringdist`, `phonics`, `PGRdup`, `fullmetaphone`, `bupaR`, `processmapR`, `edeaR`, `processcheckR` | Rule books, Benford's Law, fuzzy matching and phonetic codes, process mining |
| VI. Modelling and Risk Scoring | `broom`, `performance`, `car`, `moderndive`, `nnet`, `rpart`, `rpart.plot`, `ranger`, `deaR`, `MatchIt`, `cobalt`, `marginaleffects`, `sandwich` | Regression, classification, efficiency and impact |
| VII. Finding Hidden Patterns | `cluster`, `factoextra`, `arules`, `forecast`, `timetk`, `zoo`, `outliers`, `AnomalyDetection`, `FNN`, `dbscan`, `isotree`, `changepoint` | Principal components, clustering, association rules, time series and anomalies |
| VIII. Beyond Tables | `tidytext`, `SnowballC`, `wordcloud`, `RColorBrewer`, `igraph`, `igraphdata`, `ggraph`, `visNetwork`, `sf`, `leaflet`, `tidygeocoder` | Text, networks, maps and geocoding |
| IX. Reporting | `gt`, `openxlsx`, `quarto` | Formatted tables, Excel working papers, rendering reports |

: Packages used in each part of the book {#tbl-packages}

`MASS`, `lattice` and `nnet`, also used in the book, come with every installation of R and need no separate installation.

## Installing the packages {#sec-packages-install}

The commands below need an internet connection, and may take a while the first time. If your office network blocks downloads, see the note on installing packages on an office network in @sec-packages-intro.

There is no need to install everything at once. Start with the first command, which is enough for Gearing Up and Part I. Then install the packages of each part when you reach it.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# To begin, and for Part I
install.packages(c("tidyverse", "conflicted", "remotes"))

# Part II, Getting Data Ready
install.packages(c("digest", "openssl", "encryptr", "readxl", "writexl", "openxlsx", "janitor", "pdftools", "tidyxl",
                   "unpivotr", "rvest", "httr2", "xml2", "stringdist", "data.table", "duckdb", "dbplyr"))

# Part III, Working with Text Fields
install.packages("rebus")

# Part IV, Exploring and Sampling
install.packages(c("scales", "ggrepel", "patchwork", "RColorBrewer", "colorspace", "psych",
                   "skimr", "GGally", "PerformanceAnalytics", "broom"))

# Part V, Forensic Tests
install.packages(c("validate", "pointblank", "benford.analysis", "kableExtra", "stringdist", "phonics", "fullmetaphone",
                   "PGRdup", "bupaR", "processmapR", "edeaR", "processcheckR"))

# Part VI, Modelling and Risk Scoring
install.packages(c("broom", "performance", "car", "moderndive", "rpart", "rpart.plot",
                   "ranger", "deaR", "MatchIt", "cobalt", "marginaleffects", "sandwich"))

# Part VII, Finding Hidden Patterns
install.packages(c("cluster", "factoextra", "arules", "forecast", "timetk", "zoo",
                   "outliers", "FNN", "dbscan", "isotree", "changepoint"))

# Part VIII, Beyond Tables
install.packages(c("tidytext", "SnowballC", "wordcloud", "RColorBrewer", "igraph",
                   "igraphdata", "ggraph", "visNetwork", "sf", "leaflet", "tidygeocoder"))

# Part IX, Reporting
install.packages(c("gt", "openxlsx", "quarto"))
```
:::


If you prefer to install everything in one go, run all the commands above one after another.

One package used in Part VII is not on CRAN, and is installed from GitHub with the package `remotes`, which the first command above installs.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Seasonal Hybrid ESD anomaly detection, by Twitter
remotes::install_github("twitter/AnomalyDetection")
```
:::


The package `fullmetaphone`, installed with Part V above, is a full implementation of the Double Metaphone algorithm keeping phonetic codes of up to 32 characters. It was developed by Atharv Tyagi and the author, and is available on CRAN. It is used in @sec-strsim, @sec-dup and @sec-linkage.

::: callout-tip
## Keeping an analysis reproducible

Packages are updated from time to time, and occasionally a function changes its behaviour. For an audit that must be reproducible, record the versions used, as shown in @sec-TIDYVE with `sessionInfo()`. For larger projects, the package `renv` keeps a separate, fixed set of package versions for each project, so that an analysis written today runs the same way next year.
:::
